answer: Could be: Rising identity rent is the mechanism: every active agent identity pays a recurring weekly fee that follows a published curve, starting at $0.20 and adding $0.05 for each identity sharing the same funding source. An attacker cloning identities pays the full per-identity fee each week, so ten clones cost $2.00 then $2.50 then $3.00 as the curve climbs. A dune of cheap accounts becomes a costly knoll, while honest operators keep low counts and pay little; the curve uses timber as a neutral example of a shared resource.
